content.text:
A user reported the following issue:
Output is not byte-deterministic. Two runs on an identical tigerbeetle tree produced different bytes — 51 relations differed, same count, after sorting. All were DATA_FLOWS where evidence.detail names an arbitrary one of several forwarded params (a -> f() vs b -> f()), i.e. Go map order leaking out. ~0.14% of records. Relation identity is stable; only the evidence payload varies. This contradicts AGENTS.md's "The same commit yields the same graph."
I'll start by locating the DATA_FLOWS evidence-detail code.

content.text:
Fixed and verified. Root cause and evidence:

## Root cause

`internal/sem/types.go:790` — the final sort in `returnFlowCalls` compared only `Name` and `EvidenceKind`, but the `flows` map it drains is keyed by **name + kind + detail**. When a function forwards several params into the same callee, those entries all share a name and kind and differ only in `Detail` — so they tied, and `sort.Slice` is not stable, so Go's randomized map iteration order decided their relative order.

Downstream, `dedupeRelations` (`provider.go:16816`) keys on `from_id + to_id + type` only and keeps the **first** record. One DATA_FLOWS edge, several competing flows to supply its evidence → whichever flow the map happened to yield first won. Exactly the reported signature: stable relation identity, varying `evidence.detail`, no count change.

## Fix

Made the comparator a total order (`Detail`, `Direction`, `Reason` as tiebreakers). One-line semantics: for `f(a, b)` the evidence now deterministically names `a`.

## Verification

Reproduced on a real repo before fixing — `cli-cli` (80,616 records), 3 extra runs against the pre-fix binary:

- run1 vs run2/3/4: **107 / 111 / 111** differing lines, and classifying them: **214/214 were `"type":"DATA_FLOWS"`**, nothing else. A representative pair flipped between `"detail":"a.Login -> actorDisplayName()"` and `"detail":"a.Name -> actorDisplayName()"` on the identical edge.

After the fix, byte-identical output across runs:

| repo | records | DATA_FLOWS | runs | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| cli-cli (Go) | 80,616 | — | 5 | all identical |
| vitejs-vite (TS/JS) | 45,027 | 1,178 | 3 | all identical |
| spring-framework (Java) | 720,348 | 3,300 | 3 | all identical |

## Guards added

- Extended `TestStreamSnapshotOrderIsDeterministic` — its fixture never exercised multi-param forwarding, which is why it missed this. Added a forwarding fixture, bumped it from 2 runs to 9 (two runs can match by luck when only a couple of orderings exist), and asserted DATA_FLOWS is actually present.
- New `TestReturnFlowCallsOrderIsTotal` — unit-level, 200 iterations, asserts the fixture really produces 3 competing flows before checking stability.

Both guards fail on the pre-fix code and pass after. Full suite (`go test ./...`), `gofmt`, and `go vet` are clean.

Two things worth noting:

- The evidence dedupe still **discards** the losing flows — `a -> f()` survives, `b -> f()` is dropped rather than merged into the evidence array. That's now deterministic but still lossy; merging evidence would change record shape and volume, so I left it alone as out of scope for a determinism bug.
- I didn't test tigerbeetle itself — no local clone, and I didn't want to fetch one without asking. The reproduction on cli-cli matches the reported signature precisely, and the fix is at the single DATA_FLOWS emitter, so it covers the reported tree.

Changes are uncommitted; tell me if you want them committed.
I approve that you clone tigerbeetle

Stacked on #72 (base: `claude/verify-gate-suite-fallback`).

A user reported that output is not byte-deterministic: two runs over an identical tigerbeetle tree produced different bytes — ~0.14% of records differed, all `DATA_FLOWS` whose `evidence.detail` named an arbitrary one of several forwarded params (`a -> f()` vs `b -> f()`). Relation identity was stable; only the evidence payload varied. This contradicts AGENTS.md's "the same commit always yields the same graph."

## Root cause

The final sort in `returnFlowCalls` (`internal/sem/types.go`) compared only `Name` and `EvidenceKind`, but the `flows` map it drains is keyed by **name + kind + detail**. When a function forwards several params into the same callee, those entries share a name and kind and differ only in `Detail` — so they tied on the comparator, and `sort.Slice` is not stable, leaving Go's randomized map iteration to decide their order.

Downstream, `dedupeRelations` keys on `from_id + to_id + type` alone and keeps the **first** record. One `DATA_FLOWS` edge, several competing flows to supply its evidence → whichever the map yielded first won.

## Fix

Make the comparator a total order (`Detail`, `Direction`, `Reason` as tiebreakers). For `f(a, b)` the evidence now deterministically names `a`.

## Verification

Reproduced on tigerbeetle@`97c7a8e` (49,625 records), then confirmed fixed:

| path | pre-fix | post-fix |
|---|---|---|
| worktree | run1 vs 2/3/4: 57 / 57 / 48 differing lines | 6 runs, one sha256 |
| committed tree (default) | run1 vs 2/3: 46 / 57 differing lines | 4 runs, byte-identical |
| sorted comparison (reporter's method) | 57 differing records, counts equal | — |

Every differing line was `"type":"DATA_FLOWS"` — 114/114 in the classified run, nothing else. By language: 55 Zig, 2 Python. Observed flips:

```
"detail":"} -> build_ci_step()"     vs  "detail":"b -> build_ci_step()"
"detail":"method -> decode()"       vs  "detail":"indent -> decode()"
"detail":"env -> get_string_utf()"  vs  "detail":"addresses_obj -> get_string_utf()"
```

The reported 51 sits in the run-to-run range (46–57); the count varies per run pair with how many ties the map order flips.

Post-fix byte-identical output also confirmed on cli-cli (Go, 80,616 records, 5 runs), vitejs-vite (TS/JS, 45,027 records, 3 runs), and spring-framework (Java, 720,348 records, 3 runs).

Also checked the cached `--head` query path via `impact`, 5 runs with a fresh cache dir each: content is stable pre- and post-fix — only the latency telemetry header (`Index: cache-miss (27080ms) | ...`) varies, which is expected.

## Tests

`TestStreamSnapshotOrderIsDeterministic` missed this because its fixture never forwarded several params into one callee, and it compared only two runs — which can match by luck when few orderings exist. Added the fixture, raised it to nine runs, asserted `DATA_FLOWS` is actually present, and added `TestReturnFlowCallsOrderIsTotal` as a unit-level guard (200 iterations, with a precondition that the fixture really produces competing flows).

Both guards fail on the pre-fix code and pass after. Full suite, `gofmt`, and `go vet` clean on this stacked base.

## Notes

- The dedupe still **discards** the losing flows rather than merging them into the evidence array — now deterministic, but still lossy. Merging would change record shape and volume, so it's out of scope here.
- Incidental: `snapshot` rejects `--head` (`snapshot received unexpected arguments: --head`); committed-tree is its default and `--worktree` is the opt-out. Passing it silently yields 0 records, which can read as a vacuous "identical". May be worth a look separately.
